Atmospheric Police: Delegated Authority in the Clean Development Mechanism\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400848669-008\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2013, 12, 31]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2307/j.ctt5hhqdr.10\", \"title\": [\"Atmospheric Police:\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2307/j.ctt5hhqdr.10\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2013, 12, 22]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.5220/0014490000004052\", \"title\": [\"Assessing Moral Frameworks for Autonomous Vehicle Decision-Making\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5220/0014490000004052\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6316039\", \"title\": [\"Delegated Brokerage in Fragmented Governance: Interpretive Authority and Regional Mediation in Initiative-Based Order\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This research develops a theory of interpretive delegation and delegated brokerage to explain how authority is redistributed under initiative-based governance in fragmented institutional environments. It argues that when major powers expand influence through broadly articulated initiatives, rather than through treaty replacement, and embed these initiatives within existing multilateral institutions, centralized interpretive control becomes structurally diluted. Because initiative principles are under-specified, partially embedded, and dependent on multi-level translation for implementation, authority over meaning is redistributed downward. This redistribution does not occur through formal contractual delegation but through structural necessity, generating what the research terms interpretive delegation. Building on this structural condition, the research introduces delegated brokerage to capture the active political process through which cohesive regional organizations convert interpretive authority into procedural leverage.
